meaning: Tell the public about something, such as a product or an event, to make them want it.
example: The new water park advertises on the side of every bus in town.
group: Adverts and platforms 广告与平台

meaning: A message that a company or group pays to show the public, to make people buy, do or think something.
example: The ice cream advert plays before every film at the cinema this summer.
group: Adverts and platforms 广告与平台
note: Also in Representation: separate entry, advertising meaning and example.

meaning: A very large board beside a road or on a building, used for showing adverts.
example: Drivers on the motorway pass a billboard with a slice of pizza as big as a house.
group: Adverts and platforms 广告与平台

meaning: An advert on television or radio.
example: The toy commercial is shown on Saturday mornings, in between the cartoons.
group: Adverts and platforms 广告与平台

meaning: A small printed sheet of paper, handed out in the street or pushed through doors, that tells people about something.
example: A flyer for the new noodle bar offers a free drink with every bowl.
group: Adverts and platforms 广告与平台

meaning: A long, narrow sign or advert, hung up outside or shown across the top of a web page.
example: A banner across the top of the football club's website shows the new team shirt.
group: Adverts and platforms 广告与平台

meaning: An advert that suddenly opens in a small new window on a screen.
example: A pop-up for cheap flights covers the news story Mia is trying to read.
group: Adverts and platforms 广告与平台

meaning: A large printed advert put up on a wall, at a bus stop or in a station.
example: The poster at the bus stop shows a glass of orange juice glowing in the morning sun.
group: Adverts and platforms 广告与平台
note: Also in Representation: separate entry, advertising meaning and example.

meaning: The large glass front of a store, where goods are set out for people walking past to see.
example: The bakery's shop window is full of cakes shaped like pumpkins for Halloween.
group: Adverts and platforms 广告与平台

meaning: A type of product made by one company, with its own name and look.
example: The trainer advert never tells us the price; it only wants us to remember the brand.
group: Brands and products 品牌与产品

meaning: The name a company gives its product, so that people can ask for it and find it.
example: The brand name 'Fizzlo' is printed in huge letters across every can of lemonade.
group: Brands and products 品牌与产品

meaning: A symbol that appears on a company's products and adverts, so that people know them at once.
example: At the end of the sportswear commercial, the screen goes black and the logo, a golden leaf, appears.
group: Brands and products 品牌与产品
note: Also in Representation: separate entry, advertising meaning and example.

meaning: Something that is made or grown to be sold.
example: In the phone advert, the product only appears in the last five seconds.
group: Brands and products 品牌与产品

meaning: The box, bag or wrapper that something comes in when you buy it.
example: The biscuits' bright yellow packaging stands out on the supermarket shelf.
group: Brands and products 品牌与产品

meaning: A small piece of paper or cloth on a product that gives its name and other information.
example: The label on the juice bottle says 'No added sugar' in big green letters.
group: Brands and products 品牌与产品

meaning: A character, often an animal, that a company or team uses to make people remember it.
example: The cereal's mascot, a cartoon owl in a red scarf, waves from the front of every box.
group: Brands and products 品牌与产品

meaning: A person who buys things from a shop or a company.
example: The supermarket's radio advert promises every customer a free coffee on Mondays.
group: Audiences and markets 受众与市场

meaning: A person who is looking around a store or a website for things to buy.
example: In the shopping centre's TV advert, smiling shoppers ride up the escalators with bags in both hands.
group: Audiences and markets 受众与市场

meaning: A lower price or an extra gift that you can only get for a short time.
example: The cinema's website has a special offer: free popcorn with every Tuesday ticket.

meaning: An amount taken off the usual price.
example: The bookshop's poster promises a 20% discount for students.
group: Persuasion 说服手法

meaning: A time when a shop sells things for less money than usual.
example: The department store's TV advert shouts 'Everything must go!' to announce its summer sale.
group: Persuasion 说服手法

meaning: The amount of money you have to pay for something.
example: The furniture shop's newspaper advert prints the price of the sofa in giant red numbers.
group: Persuasion 说服手法

meaning: A small amount of a product given away for nothing, so that people can try it.
example: Every copy of the magazine comes with a free sample of face cream stuck to the cover.
group: Persuasion 说服手法

meaning: A famous person, especially from sport, music, film or TV.
example: The chocolate advert uses a celebrity: a world-famous tennis player eats a bar after winning a match.
group: Persuasion 说服手法

meaning: A short phrase that a brand uses again and again, so that people remember it.
example: The toothpaste's slogan, 'Brighter every morning', comes at the end of all its adverts.

meaning: The biggest words in a printed advert, which the reader sees first.

meaning: The main idea that an advert wants people to remember.

meaning: Easy to remember, often so easy that you can't stop thinking about it.
example: The song in the burger advert is so catchy that it stays in your head for days.

meaning: A short, simple tune with words, used in an advert on radio or TV.
example: The carpet shop's jingle is so simple that children sing it in the playground.
